 Judgment

These appeals by the petitioner and by the Insurance Company are directed against the judgment and award dated 21-12-2017 passed I MVC No.98/2015 by the learned I Additional Senior Civil Judge and V MACT, Davanagere, whereby the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.3,97,193/- on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 15.05.2014 at about 9.15 a.m. when he was proceeding on the left side of the road in his motor bike bearing Reg.No. KA 17/EC-1172 from SSIMS hospital towards NC: 2023:KHC:43914 Davanagere City via Nituvalli road, near SSIMS hospital on NH-4 underbridge, the respondent No.1 being the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No. MH-46-F 3702 came from TV station road towards NH 4 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle, resulting in fall and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to SSIMS hospital Davanagere wherein he took treatment as inpatient, underwent surgery and discharged from the hospital.
Thereafter, he got admitted to the Navodaya hospital for skin grafting and took the followup treatment at Basaveshwar Health Centre and private hospitals at Davanagere.
It was the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy working as Clerk in the Judicial Department and getting monthly income of Rs.13,900/-.
The accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1 and Davanagere Rural Police have registered the case against the respondent No.1 in Crime No.58/2014.

The respondent No.1 and 2 being the driver cum owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the NC: 2023:KHC:43914 compensation and prayed to award adequate compensation.
3. On issuance of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear and as such, he was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company has appeared through his counsel and filed the objection statement contending that the petition is not maintainable in law or on facts and denied the petition averments and its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It was further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license,
and violated the terms and conditions of the policy and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW1 and Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 were marked.
The official of the respondent No.2 was examined as RW1 and Ex.R1 to Ex.R19 were marked in evidence.

After hearing the arguments on both the sides, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.3,97,193/- under different heads as below:
 Pain and suffering Rs.70,000/-

Medical bills Rs.91,979/-
Loss of income during laid up Rs.1,35,214/- period Loss of amenities conveyance Rs.60,000/- food and nourishment and attendant charges Disfiguration of left leg Rs.40,000/-

Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the Insurance Company is in appeal before this Court in MFA No.3239/2018 assailing the liability fastened upon it despite it being able to prove that the respondent No.1- driver of lorry, was not having a valid driving licence.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award the petitioner also has filed MFA No.8556/2019 contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and adequate compensation was not awarded to him.
In MFA No.8556/2019 notice to respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle is dispensed with.

However, in MFA No.3239/2018 notice to respondent No.2 owner of the vehicle is held sufficient by vide order dated 27.06.2022.
8.
The arguments by learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2-insurance company were heard.

Learned counsel Sri. B.Pradeep appearing for the appellant/respondent No.2-insurance company contends that respondent No.2 has established that the respondent No.1 was not having a valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

He contends that the endorsement issued by the District Transport Officer of Amritsar shows that the driving licence which was provided to the police bearing No.DL 22467 in the name of Manjith Singh was in fact not issued by his office and therefore it is a fake one.

Therefore he contends that in view of the said endorsement appearing on Ex.R10, the Tribunal should NC:
2023:KHC:43914 have held that the respondent-insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
9. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner contends that the Tribunal has not considered the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the proper perspective.

She contends that the petitioner had sustained abrasion over right knee measuring  x  cm, fracture of left 2nd and 4th rib, fracture of left ankle comminited lower 1/3rd and fracture of both the bones of the left leg i.e., tibia and fibula.
She contends that it was a compound type II fracture of tibia and fibula, Distal 1/3rd of left side with fracture of the clavicle as well as fracture of the 2nd and 4th rib.

These injuries were not properly appreciated by the Tribunal and the petitioner was working in judicial department and he had to remain absent for considerable period of time loosing his salary Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd vs A.P.Jagannath on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126544329/

NC: 2023:KHC:43914 It is contended that the Tribunal should have awarded higher compensation under different heads.
10. The first contention to be considered by this Court is in respect of the liability of the respondent No.2- insurance company.

The police records produced by the petitioner at Ex.P2 show that the Davangere traffic police has registered the case in respect of the said accident and found that the driver of the offending lorry i.e. MH.46.F.3702 [Multi Axle] Ashok Leyland heavy goods vehicle was at fault.

It is to be noted that the charge sheet produced by the petitioner at Ex.P7 show that the driver of the lorry was not prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act i.e., for non possession of the valid driving licence.
It is to be noted that a copy of the driving licence which was furnished by the police was also produced by the petitioner.

In the said driving licence, which was issued in favour of Manjit Singh S/o Pal Singh, driving licence - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 No.9110DL O.No.22487/NASR was issued in the name of the respondent No.1.
11.

On the other hand the respondent No.2- insurance company has led the evidence of its official as RW1 and he has produced the various notices issued by it to the respondent No.1 seeking to productin the driving licence of the driver, as on the date of the accident.
The registered letters issued by the insurance company from Ex.R3 to R9 show that these notices issued were returned to the insurance company as the addressee was not found in the said address.
It is pertinent to note that the notice issued to the respondent No.1 by this Court has returned as not claimed.
In the ultimate result, the notice issued by this Court, the Tribunal as well as Insurance company was not positively served upon the respondent No.1.
The Ex.R10 is the endorsement issued by the District Transport Officer, Amritsar.

The said endorsement shows that the said Manjit Singh S/o Pal Singh was not issued with any driving licence by his office and the copy of the driving - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 licence which is accompanied to Ex.R10 show that in fact the said driving licence was issued by DTO, Amritsar.
When there is clear endorsement by the issuing authority, it is evident that the said respondent No.1 was not having a valid driving licence.

12. It is pertinent to note that on the part of the petitioner he has made all the efforts to produce the driving licence which was available with him and the respondent No.2 also had made all his efforts to secure the driving licence.
But the respondent No.1 who was also the owner of the lorry has not bothered to produce the driving licence.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that for no fault of the petitioner, he should not suffer when the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 is admitted by it.

In this regard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has placed reliance on the decision rendered in the case of Pappu v.

sentences.text: The summary of our findings to the various issues as raised in these petitions is as follows:

( i) Chapter XI of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 providing compulsory insurance of vehicles against third-party risks is a social welfare legislation to extend relief by compensation to victims of accidents caused by use of motor vehicles.
The provisions of compulsory insurance coverage of all vehicles are with this paramount object and the provisions of the Act have to be so interpreted as to effectuate the said object.

(ii) An insurer is entitled to raise a defence in a claim petition filed under Section 163-A or Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, inter alia, in terms of Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of the said Act.

(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g. disqualification of driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of Section 149, has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

(2018) 3 SCC 208 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 (iv) Insurance companies, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also establish "breach" on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof where for would be on them.
(v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how the said burden would be discharged, inasmuch as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstance of each case.

6 (vi)

sentences.text: Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose"
and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insurer under Section 149(2) of the Act.

(vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving licence produced by the driver (a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfil the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.
(viii)-(ix) ***

( x) Where on adjudication of the claim under the Act the Tribunal arrives at a conclusion that the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provisions of Section 149(2) read with sub-section (7), as interpreted by this Court above, the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which it has been compelled to pay to the third-party under the award of the Tribunal.

Such determination of claim by the Tribunal will be enforceable and the money found due to the insurer from the insured will be recoverable on a certificate issued by the Tribunal to the Collector in the same manner under Section 174 of the Act as - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 arrears of land revenue.

The certificate will be issued for the recovery as arrears of land revenue only if, as required by sub-section (3) of Section 168 of the Act the insured fails to deposit the amount awarded in favour of the insurer within thirty days from the date of announcement of the award by the Tribunal.

(xi) The provisions contained in sub-section (4) with the proviso thereunder and sub-section (5)
which are intended to cover specified contingencies mentioned therein to enable the insurer to recover the amount paid under the contract of insurance on behalf of the insured can be taken recourse to by the Tribunal and be extended to claims and defences of the insurer against the insured by relegating them to the remedy before regular court in cases where on given facts and circumstances adjudication of their claims inter se might delay the adjudication of the claims of the victims."
(emphasis supplied)

sentences.text: In the present case, the owner of the vehicle (Respondent 1) had produced the insurance certificate indicating that Vehicle No. DIL 5955 was comprehensively insured by Respondent 2 (insurance company) for unlimited liability.

Applying the dictum in National Insurance Co. Ltd. , to subserve the ends of justice, the insurer (Respondent 2) shall pay the claim amount awarded by the Tribunal to the appellants in the first instance, with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle (Respondent 1) in accordance with law."

13. In view of the above decision, when the respondent No.2 has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provisions contending Section 149(2) R/w Sub Section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the respondent No.2 should be directed to pay the - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 compensation to the petitioner with liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1.

The petitioner has discharged his burden as required under law and therefore the interse dispute between the respondent Nos.1 and 2 in respect of violation of the terms and conditions of the policy should not affect the rights of the petitioner herein.

Hence, the respondent No.2-insurance company has to be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner with the liberty to recover same from respondent No.1.
14.

The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2-insurance company has placed reliance on the decision in the case of Joyeeta Bose and others V/s Venkateshan and others2, and therefore the rate of interest has to be awarded at 6% per annum.

sentences.text: 15. Coming to the quantum of the compensation amount, it is evident that the petitioner had sustained the injuries as mentioned above.

The discharge summary produced at Ex.P8 and Ex.P9 and the wound certificate MFA No.5896/2018 & Conn.Matters DD 24/8/2020 - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:43914 produced at Ex.P1 coupled with the evidence of the PW1 show that the petitioner had sustained severe injuries as narrated supra.
Therefore, there is a need for reassessment of the compensation to be awarded to the petitioner.
In considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded under the head of pain and suffering has to be enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.91,979/- and he was also a Government servant and he is at liberty to seek reimbursement from department.
Hence, the sum of Rs.91,979/- as awarded by the Tribunal has to be maintained.
The petitioner was awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards food nourishment, conveyance charges etc.

It has to be enhanced to Rs.70,000/- (a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards nourishment, conveyance and attendants charges and Rs.40,000/- in respect of loss of amenities in life).
16.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,35,214/- towards loss of income during laid up - 17 - Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd vs A.P.Jagannath on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126544329/
8 NC: 2023:KHC:43914 period.

sentences.text: This amount was arrived at on the basis of the earned leave applied by him for a period of 224 days and in view of the pay slip and medical certificate produced by him at Ex.P17.
Therefore, the compensation awarded under the loss of income during the laid up period is also proper and correct and no interference is required for the same.
17. The petitioner has produced the photographs of his disfigured leg at Ex.P15 and Ex.P16.
This clearly shows that the ankle of the left leg of the petitioner had crushed and there is a disfiguration and it appears that it has been defused.
However, no compensation under the head of loss of earning capacity could be granted since he has continued in service.
Under these circumstances, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of disfiguration of the left leg needs to be enhanced to Rs.80,000/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.4,77,193/-
under different heads as below:
- 18 -  NC: 2023:KHC:43914

Pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-
Medical bills Rs.91,979/-
Loss of amenities, food, nourishment, Rs.70,000/-
conveyance and attendant charges Loss of income during laid up period 1,35,214/-
Disfiguration of left leg Rs.80,000/-
Total Rs.4,77,193/-
18.
Hence, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Both the appeals are allowed in part.
The petitioner is entitled for a  compensation of Rs.4,77,193/- instead of Rs.3,97,193/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its deposit before the Tribunal

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks and is at liberty to recover the said amount from the respondent No.1 by way of execution of this award.

Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd vs A.P.Jagannath on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126544329/
6 (vi)
Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose"
and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insurer under Section 149(2) of the Act.
Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd vs A.P.Jagannath on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126544329/
7 19.
The petitioner has discharged his burden as required under law and therefore the interse dispute between the respondent Nos.1 and 2 in respect of violation of the terms and conditions of the policy should not affect the rights of the petitioner herein.
Hence, the respondent No.2-insurance company has to be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner with the liberty to recover same from respondent No.1.
14.
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.91,979/- and he was also a Government servant and he is at liberty to seek reimbursement from department.
opennyai_summary.issue: (vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving licence produced by the driver (a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfil the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded under the head of pain and suffering has to be enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Hence, the sum of Rs.91,979/- as awarded by the Tribunal has to be maintained.
The petitioner was awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards food nourishment, conveyance charges etc.
It has to be enhanced to Rs.70,000/- (a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards nourishment, conveyance and attendants charges and Rs.40,000/- in respect of loss of amenities in life).
16.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,35,214/- towards loss of income during laid up - 17 - Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd vs A.P.Jagannath on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126544329/
8 NC: 2023:KHC:43914 period.
However, no compensation under the head of loss of earning capacity could be granted since he has continued in service.
Under these circumstances, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of disfiguration of the left leg needs to be enhanced to Rs.80,000/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.4,77,193/-
under different heads as below:
- 18 -  NC: 2023:KHC:43914
Pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-
Medical bills Rs.91,979/-
Loss of amenities, food, nourishment, Rs.70,000/-
conveyance and attendant charges Loss of income during laid up period 1,35,214/-
Disfiguration of left leg Rs.80,000/-
Total Rs.4,77,193/-
18.
Hence, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following:
ORDER Both the appeals are allowed in part.
The petitioner is entitled for a  compensation of Rs.4,77,193/- instead of Rs.3,97,193/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its deposit before the Tribunal
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks and is at liberty to recover the said amount from the respondent No.1 by way of execution of this award.
The amount which is in deposit before this court is ordered to be transmitted by the Tribunal immediately.
The terms and conditions imposed by the Tribunal in respect of fixed deposit remained unaltered.
